This is a bail application U/S.483 of the BNSS by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Dhenkanal Sadar PS Case No. 814 of 2024 corresponding to GR Case No.1452 of 2024 pending in the Court of learned SDJM, Dhenkanal for commission of offences punishable U/Ss. 452/376(D)/
376(2)(n)/ 506 of IPC, on the main allegation of committing Gang Rape upon the victim.
3.

Heard, Mr. Manoranjan Das, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. M.R. Patra, learned Addl.
Public Prosecutor in the matter and perused the record.

4. No doubt, the bail has been sought for to the Petitioner mainly on the ground of parity and consensual relationship between two adults, but fact remains that there is allegation against the Petitioner for committing Gang Rape upon the victim.

According to Sec. 114-A of the Indian Evidence Act/120 Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, in a prosecution for Gang Rape, the Court shall presume that the victim has not consented for such intercourse, once the intercourse is found established in evidence and the victim has said that she has not consented for such intercourse.

For the sake of argument, accepting for a moment, but not admitting the submission of the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the relationship between the parties is consensual in nature, it appears that since the victim has deposed in evidence that she has never consented for intercourse,
the Court has no other option left, but to presume that the intercourse made on the victim is without consent.

sentences.text:
In the aforesaid backdrop and after having considered the rival submissions and on going through the materials placed on record together with the evidence of witnesses, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the Petitioner nor considers it proper to extend the principle of parity to the Petitioner,
since the offence alleged against the Petitioner is heinous and serious and it defies all logic and dignity of a woman.
Hence, the bail application of the petitioner stands rejected.

It is, however, clarified that the learned trial Court shall not be influenced by any observation made by this Court in this order, since this Court has purely discussed the matter on academic purpose on the submission of the learned counsel for the Petitioner.
6. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.

7. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
According to Sec. 114-A of the Indian Evidence Act/120 Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, in a prosecution for Gang Rape, the Court shall presume that the victim has not consented for such intercourse, once the intercourse is found established in evidence and the victim has said that she has not consented for such intercourse.
For the sake of argument, accepting for a moment, but not admitting the submission of the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the relationship between the parties is consensual in nature, it appears that since the victim has deposed in evidence that she has never consented for intercourse,
the Court has no other option left, but to presume that the intercourse made on the victim is without consent.
In the aforesaid backdrop and after having considered the rival submissions and on going through the materials placed on record together with the evidence of witnesses, this Court is not inclined to grant bail to the Petitioner nor considers it proper to extend the principle of parity to the Petitioner,
since the offence alleged against the Petitioner is heinous and serious and it defies all logic and dignity of a woman.
